ELEPHANT DUNG GIN

By: Ntokozo Miya | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Picture this: You are at a bar and feeling adventurous so you ask the barman to surprise you and he does – with a glass of gin infused with elephant dung. What's your next move?

Unique Selling Point:
We not only interview the founders of Indlovu Gin, an elephant dung infused beverage, but we also take the viewer on a visually compelling journey – from dung collection to manufacturing plant to a glass of gin at a bar.

Summary:
In 2018, animal and nature lovers, Paula and Lesley Ansley were drinking gin and tonic on a safari holiday when the idea for gin made from elephant dung was born. The couple worked to make the dream a reality and three years later, the product is sold both locally and internationally, and has bagged a Double Gold Award at the South African Craft Awards.

The drink is described as “a full-bodied highly aromatic gin with grassy earthy notes. It is good with Indian Tonic, but it is even better sipped neat with chocolate or coffee on the side.”

The elephant dung gin project is essentially a collaboration between the founding couple and HERD.

Further information:
The gin is sold online on platforms such as Takealot and Makro Online. It is also available at selected retail stores. It sells for R545 a bottle and 15% of the proceeds is reserved for the HERD elephant orphanage. (These are the caregivers for Khanyisa, the albino elephant that we've had on Carte Blanche.)

The business also produces another elephant gin called Jabu Gin – it is unique as it made specifically with dung collected from the elephant at the Jabulani Safari. Jabu Gin is sold to visitors at the reserve's lodge. All proceeds from Jabu Gin go towards HERD.

The gin is exported to Europe, Asia and North America.

FINAL SCRIPT - ELEPHANT DUNG GIN



AUDIO

VO – We’re following a bush trail. But, we’re not hot on the heels of poachers, illegal hunters or bandits.


We’re at Jabulani Safari on Limpopo’s Kapama Private Game Reserve, on an entirely different quest: today we’re on the lookout for dung. Specifically, elephant dung.

LINK – Majestic and revered, their size puts fear even in lions. But who would have thought that from the guts of African elephants could come this – an elephant dung infused gin.

VO – In early 2018, Western Cape couple Leslie and Paula Ansley were struck by an unusual business opportunity while on safari.

PAULA ANSLEY – INDLOVU GIN CO-FOUNDER



I suddenly was like: “Could you use elephant dung in the production of gin?”

VO – Back from their trip, they called a friend at a wildlife resort to find out.

PAULA ANSLEY – INDLOVU GIN CO-FOUNDER



PAULA – And I just said, would it be possible to obtain a couple of balls of dung, and then she said, 'I'll courier it to you.'



CLAIRE – She couriered dung?!?



PAULA – (nods) Thank you very much.

VO – Before revealing what the substance was, they then asked friend and renowned distiller, Roger Jorgensen, if it could be infused with gin.

PAULA ANSLEY – INDLOVU GIN CO-FOUNDER



PAULA – Then he tastes it (laughs) and then he goes: “You can definitely make gin from this but what is it?” I went: “Well, it's dried and sanitised elephant dung.” And then you kind of wait...



CLAIRE – (exclaims and laughs)



PAULA - ...for the penny to drop and whether he's going to say: “Okay, get out of here now, you really are crazy.”

VO – He didn't think they were crazy at all, and the first bottle of Indlovu Gin, made with dung collected from reserves across the country, was sold in late 2018.

LESLIE ANSLEY – INDLOVU GIN CO-FOUNDER



When we made this gin, one of the things we were very determined about was that it had to contribute in some way. We donate 15% of our profits to H.E.R.D.

VO – H.E.R.D is a charity looking after orphaned elephants. The Ansley’s second offering, Jabu Gin, is infused with dung gathered exclusively from their elephants at Jabulani Safari.



Initially, H.E.R.D. Founder and Jabulani Safari owner, Adine Roode, was skeptical.

ADINE ROODE – H.E.R.D. FOUNDER & JABULANI SAFARI OWNER



I have scooped poop a lot so your hands, everything smells. I wasn't sure about this gin and how it will taste and smell.



VO – But, tasting it for the first time, she was pleasantly surprised.



But, there’s a lot more at stake than cocktails and dung: this drink is helping support elephants orphaned by poachers at a time the scourge is showing little sign of being brought under control.



The Covid pandemic has crippled ivory supply networks, but groups fighting international organised crime say demand is still alarmingly high.



There’s been a spike in the black market ivory price: it’s nearly doubled from around twelve thousand rands ($750 converted to rands – R11 537.15) per kilogram to more than 23 thousand ($1 500 converted to rands – R23 074.31)in 2020.



And, as lockdowns ease, poaching is expected to intensify, endangering many of South Africa's roughly 26 thousand elephants.



It’s bad news for conservationists already spending thousands of rands to secure elephants in protected areas.



As the hunger for ivory grows, Roode is bracing for another increase in elephant orphans.

ADINE ROODE – H.E.R.D. FOUNDER & JABULANI SAFARI OWNER



CLAIRE – How does H.E.R.D. actually benefit from the gin?



ADINE – A lot of the expenses goes into staff salaries. That is one of the biggest costs but then also, the food costs, all the milk supplements that we have to buy.

VO – Taking care of young calves is particularly expensive.



In 2020, we introduced you to Khanyisa, an orphaned albino baby elephant who was found with injuries caused by a snare. (CB – FEBRUARY 2020)

DR PETER ROGERS – WILDLIFE VETERINARIAN (CB – FEBRUARY 2020)



She came in with 3 factors that were against her. Firstly, this terrible snare wound. Secondly, her colour is very susceptible to the sun and being sun-burned. And then thirdly, to get her into the right milk formula because it varies from one individual to the next.

VO – As it happens, dung was central to Khanyisa's recovery.

DR PETER ROGERS – WILDLIFE VETERINARIAN (CB – FEBRUARY 2020)



We take the fresh dung and we actually squeeze it out. The fluid in the dung contains the natural micro-organisms that you find in an elephant gut. They call it transfornation - where you are actually supplementing the gut with natural bacteria.

VO – And what is gin-making without a desire to supplement the gut? And here, they have the same interest as Khanyisa in the raw material. We’re on a dung collection outing with expert animal tracker, Shepherd Nkomazana. They might be familiar with people, but rescued elephants are still dangerous.

SHEPHERD NKOMAZANA – TRACKER - A7SIII_2668



SHEPHERD - I would suggest that we stay closer to each other. No one is taking his or her own direction otherwise you might bump into an elephant because remember, they still remain wild animals.

CLAIRE – What are we looking for this morning, Leslie? What do you want us to find?

LESLIE - We need fresh elephant dung ... What we don't want is the elephant dung like that, which is old and has been here for a long time.

VO – It appears we’re getting closer.

SHEPHERD NKOMAZANA – TRACKER



SHEPHERD – Elephants are the only animals that will feed on the bark of certain trees so you see, he just chewed off the bark because the bark which contains a lot of moisture and minerals as well.



CLAIRE – Broken branches everywhere... (natsound as they walk in the bush)



SHEPERD – There is an elephant.



CLAIRE – Ha!



LESLIE – Fantastic!



SHEPERD – And there's another one behind him.

VO – Minutes later, we hit pay dirt.

LESLIE ANSLEY – INDLOVU GIN CO-FOUNDER



This is exactly what we're looking for and you can smell that...



(Claire smells dung)



LESLIE – It's just the veld.

VO – We get down and dirty.

CLAIRE



Yo, these things are heavy, guys! (natsound) Not even the one hand is big enough.

LINK – We've been collecting dung for a few minutes now and this is how much we have managed to bag, not nearly enough for an Indlovu production cycle, but I think I've earned a shot.

VO – Later, Leslie shows us how we go from this (pile of dung) to this (bottle of gin).



The unique gin recipe was developed on this copper still, using cane spirit as the base alcohol, and berries and citrus for flavour.

LESLIE ANSLEY – INDLOVU GIN CO-FOUNDER



So you'd place your base alcohol, your cane spirit in the still, and you'd then put the botanicals in the net and you'd seal it.

VO – If we weren't in the bush, we'd light a flame to heat the alcohol. The steam draws out the flavours and the gin drips into the collection cup. As for the special ingredient...

LESLIE ANSLEY – INDLOVU GIN CO-FOUNDER



CLAIRE – Tell me the difference between this and that?



LESLIE – This is dung that we haven't even washed yet. It's still bound a bit. So it's almost like the dirt is acting as a glue within that. This is the elephant dung that we've washed and it's a beautiful fluffy materal.



CLAIRE – It's so light.



LESLIE – It is. We almost make a teabag. And we place this into the tea bag and drop it into the gin, and we let it infuse directly into the gin.

VO – With this recipe, the Ansley's were going for a smooth, liquor with an earthy aroma and hints of the various botanicals favoured by elephants, such as the bark of marula trees.

LINK – (Claire thanks the waiter delivering her drink) What may have seemed like a gimmick at first, has surpassed all expectations. Indlovu Gin is now recognised as a top player in a saturated, competitive craft gin market. Cheers!

VO – The couple's gamble paid off: by 2019 their gin was already winning awards. But, there have been some hurdles along the way.

LESLIE ANSLEY – INDLOVU GIN CO-FOUNDER



When we brought out our pink gin, we brought that out in March and then we had the first hard lockdown in April. And then we brought out our citrus gin in November and then we had the next hard lockdown in December. So we've decided, for the sake of the country, we are not going to bring out a new gin this year.



CLAIRE – Thank you. (Laughs all around) I have found them, I have for the reasons for alcohol bans.

VO – Adine says the gin is an eccentric take on elephant conservation but she is grateful for the income which funds a lot of H.E.R.D.'s research.

ADINE ROODE – H.E.R.D. FOUNDER & JABULANI SAFARI OWNER



For 2022, we'll have to look: 'Is it possible maybe to split some of the group members because as the herd grows, you need to look at other options.

VO – Khanyisa, now two years old, is one of the orphans benefitting from the collaboration between H.E.R.D. and the distillers.

ADINE ROODE – H.E.R.D. FOUNDER & JABULANI SAFARI OWNER



CLAIRE – Now that we're here, we can't not ask you about how Khanyisa is doing.



ADINE – She's a bubble of energy and this whole herd accepted her. She's actually the one that everyone comes to during the day and spend some time with her. She's doing amazing.

VO – And, her dung is also among the stockpile infused in Indlovu gin.

LESLIE ANSLEY – INDLOVU GIN CO-FOUNDER – FX3:2011



It's a wonderful model - that the elephants provide dung and we collect the dung and we make the gin. And then the gin sells and we give back to the elephants.



PROMO 1



VO - When we're in the bush it's often to search for poachers, vehicle thieves and corrupt border officials. But this time, we're looking for something completely different.



LESLIE ANSLEY – INDLOVU GIN CO-FOUNDER



We need fresh elephant dung ... What we don't want is the elephant dung like that, which is old and has been here for a long time.



A couple shows us how they use dung for a uniquely South African product.



PROMO 2



Elephant dung is a versatile material used to make soap, paper and compost. Conservationists say liquid from the dung can be a lifeline if one is stranded in the wild with no water. But an adventurous couple has gone a step further and is using dung for a beverage with an earthy taste to it.



PROMO 3 – 11 secs



An adventurous couple distils a smooth, golden liquor with an earthy aroma and hints of local botanicals such as the marula tree – but what's the secret ingredient for their unique gin?



PROMO 4 – 21 secs – Don't cover with viz - Extra promo editorial team to decide which they go with



LINK – Ordinarily, a Carte Blanche cocktail consists of a shot of skepticism, a dash of curiosity and a splash of adventure but a local couple took us on a unique taste experience – they show us how they go from this lump of elephant dung to a refreshing, gin and tonic.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Picture this: You are at a bar and feeling adventurous so you ask the barman to surprise you and he does – with a glass of gin infused with elephant dung. What's your next move?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We not only interview the founders of Indlovu Gin, an elephant dung infused beverage, but we also take the viewer on a visually compelling journey – from dung collection to manufacturing plant to a glass of gin at a bar.
metadata.Summary: In 2018, animal and nature lovers, Paula and Lesley Ansley were drinking gin and tonic on a safari holiday when the idea for gin made from elephant dung was born. The couple worked to make the dream a reality and three years later, the product is sold both locally and internationally, and has bagged a Double Gold Award at the South African Craft Awards. The drink is described as “a full-bodied highly aromatic gin with grassy earthy notes. It is good with Indian Tonic, but it is even better sipped neat with chocolate or coffee on the side.” The elephant dung gin project is essentially a collaboration between the founding couple and HERD.
metadata.Further information: The gin is sold online on platforms such as Takealot and Makro Online. It is also available at selected retail stores. It sells for R545 a bottle and 15% of the proceeds is reserved for the HERD elephant orphanage. (These are the caregivers for Khanyisa, the albino elephant that we've had on Carte Blanche.) The business also produces another elephant gin called Jabu Gin – it is unique as it made specifically with dung collected from the elephant at the Jabulani Safari. Jabu Gin is sold to visitors at the reserve's lodge. All proceeds from Jabu Gin go towards HERD. The gin is exported to Europe, Asia and North America.
